analysis: The PR changes documentation only. docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 47-54) now says standalone preload runs an excluded load-time shape warmup: a shader-cache probe, plus shape cells after a new install or a macOS/MLX kernel update. A 5-second sweep tick warms deferred engines, and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP=0 disables it. docs/reference/configuration.md line 414 adds the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP variable. It accepts 0/false/no/off to disable and `always` to skip the probe, and it is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The docs say it trains no rate or counter. No authentication, authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, coordinator wire protocol, billing or prefix-cache storage behavior is changed or documented as changed. The T-041 TTFT-oracle and prefix-cache surface is not touched by this text. The warmup uses synthetic shape probes, so it does not appear to carry consumer prompt data (A-001). I did not see the implementing code in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift or the sweep tick, so I cannot verify that warmup inputs are synthetic, that the warmup is bounded to the documented 20 seconds, or that a request preempts it. The `always` and `0` modes are operator-local controls, and the docs say nothing about them affecting the coordinator or attestation. Remaining question for deeper review, if any: confirm in the implementation that the warmup does not populate or donate to the encrypted SSD prefix cache or use real tenant prompts. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. The configuration.md patch excerpt is truncated, but the changed-range map is complete and shows a single added line.
